themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 4.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 233% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting rapid pavement degradation or a sudden reporting wave that warrants investigation into whether recent weather, construction, or deferred maintenance is accelerating street-level safety hazards.
evidence: 15 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5-complaint weekly baseline (233% spike, z-score 5.42)
Spike occurred after recent heavy weather and sustained construction activity in Central Harlem
Aligns with 459 building permit filings in last 90 days, including 5 demolitions that may be destabilizing streets
reporting_angles: Are recent demolitions and alterations destabilizing adjacent sidewalks and creating trip hazards?
Is the Department of Transportation responding to these complaints, and what is the typical repair timeline?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 6 TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 0.1-complaint weekly average—a 4,700% spike (z-score: 17.76, the highest anomaly in the dataset)—indicating a sudden flood of posters, stickers, or signage covering neighborhood storefronts and infrastructure that has not been addressed.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (4,700% spike, z-score 17.76—highest severity signal)
Spike is the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset, suggesting either coordinated posting activity or sudden enforcement/reporting change
Related to broader environment/order concerns: simultaneous spikes in litter basket requests and graffiti complaints
reporting_angles: Is this a coordinated campaign (political, commercial, or gang-related) or isolated incidents?
What triggers the spike—enforcement change, community reporting campaign, or actual new posters?

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a 0.4-complaint weekly average—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 9.55)—revealing residents perceive insufficient trash receptacles or are newly motivated to report, possibly driven by concurrent spikes in graffiti and sidewalk complaints suggesting neighborhood disorder.
evidence: 5 litter basket complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4-complaint weekly baseline (1,233% spike, z-score 9.55)
Converges with graffiti spike (7 complaints last week, 833% increase) and sidewalk complaints, forming a 'broken windows' pattern
Suggests residents perceive public space degradation and are actively seeking city services
reporting_angles: Are certain blocks or neighborhoods disproportionately underserved with trash receptacles?
Is the spike driven by residents' reaction to visible disorder, or is city underinvestment in sanitation infrastructure real?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 7 LAST WEEK from a 0.8-complaint weekly average—an 833% increase (z-score: 4.81)—indicating either a new vandalism campaign or surge in community reporting that aligns with simultaneous spikes in illegal posting and sidewalk complaints, suggesting coordinated neighborhood disorder.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints last week vs. 0.8-complaint weekly baseline (833% spike, z-score 4.81)
Part of broader 'disorder convergence': illegal posting (4,700% spike), litter basket requests (1,233% spike), and sidewalk complaints (233% spike) all elevated
Suggests either organized vandalism campaign or sudden catalyst driving resident frustration with street conditions
reporting_angles: Is there a visible gang tag or political message pattern behind the graffiti?
Are Parks and Recreation and Sanitation resources sufficient to respond to this spike?

themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 8 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.5-complaint weekly average—a 1,500% spike (z-score: 5.67)—suggesting either intensified city enforcement against street vendors or sudden resident complaints about vendor activity, warranting investigation into whether this reflects policy changes or neighborhood tensions.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (1,500% spike, z-score 5.67)
Spike predates litter and sidewalk complaints by approximately 1 week, suggesting vending activity may be related to broader street conditions concerns
No recent news coverage or ULURP applications directly addressing vending policy, limiting context
reporting_angles: Has NYPD or Parks Enforcement intensified vendor crackdowns in Central Harlem recently?
Are residents complaining about vendor behavior (blocking sidewalks, hygiene) or enforcement itself?
